description:
src/methods/metadata.rs — all five 'async fn' methods (metadata_get, metadata_changes, metadata_set, metadata_query, metadata_query_changes) return futures whose Send/Sync bounds depend on the inner JmapClient. Neither the method doc-comments nor the SessionClient doc-comment state the contract:

- Are the returned futures Send? A caller using tokio::spawn / smol::spawn needs Send.
- Is SessionClient itself Send + Sync? If the inner JmapClient holds a non-Send field (e.g. an Rc, a !Send transport), then SessionClient is not Send either.

The current implementation appears to be Send + Sync (HTTP clients are typically Arc-based), but the contract is not promised by the public API. A future jmap-base-client revision that adds a !Send field (debug counters, single-threaded transport) would silently break every multi-threaded caller — and the contract did not preclude it.

This is a concurrency-contract gap per the api-contract,underspecified checklist. Two fixes:

1. Document in the SessionClient doc-comment that SessionClient is Send + Sync (and assert via 'fn assert_send_sync<T: Send + Sync>() {} assert_send_sync::<SessionClient>();' in a #[test]).
2. Document on each async fn that the returned future is Send when …

Recommendation: (1). Pin the contract via a static assertion test, AND state it in the doc-comment. The static assertion makes a future regression (someone makes JmapClient !Send) a compile error in this crate instead of a silent contract violation that only manifests for downstream multi-task callers.

Workspace-wide: same gap exists on canonical mail-client SessionClient. Propagate.
title: Async method Send/Sync contract not documented
